slides.title: Angles in Standard Position
text: Standard Position: An angle with its vertex at the origin and its initial side along the positive x-axis.
Terminal side: the ray after rotation
Initial side: always on the positive x-axis

slides.title: Coterminal Angles — Degrees
text: Coterminal Angles: Angles that share the same terminal side. Found by adding/subtracting 360°.
Formula: θ ± 360° · n (n = any positive integer)
Every angle has infinitely many coterminal angles.

slides.title: Coterminal Angles — Radians
text: Test Prep: Be comfortable finding coterminal angles for radians like 9π/7 — this appears on Test 3, Problem 2b.

slides.title: Sketching Angles with |θ| > 360°
text: Strategy: Subtract (or add) 360° until the angle is between 0° and 360°, then sketch that coterminal angle.
Terminal side is in Quadrant II
Terminal side is in Quadrant IV

slides.title: Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions
text: Quotient: tan A = sin A / cos A
